title: Guide - Grief and Comfort - God is close

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, slow and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Grief and Comfort. <short pause> This practice is called God Is Close. <short pause> There's very little for you to do here. <short pause> Mostly, we are going to let you be held... and pray the words you may be too tired to find.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Lean back into whatever can take your weight. <short pause> A cushion, a wall, the seat beneath you. <short pause> If it helps, wrap something around your shoulders. <short pause> Let your breath be small, if small is all there is. <short pause> You don't have to breathe deeply to be loved.

Loss changes the size of a house. <short pause> The rooms grow larger, and much too quiet. <short pause> You reach for the phone, to tell them something, and then you remember. <short pause> And in that remembering, you can feel more alone than you knew a person could be. <short pause> Even God can seem to have stepped out of the room.

There is a psalm of David that speaks straight into that room. <short pause> It doesn't say that God waits for us to recover, and then draws near. <short pause> It tells us where He already is. <short pause> It is Psalm thirty-four, verse eighteen.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Nigh. <short pause> It's an old word for near. <short pause> Near, as in within reach. <short pause> Near, as in close enough to hear what is said under the breath. <short pause> And near to whom? <short pause> To the broken heart. <short pause> The very thing that makes you feel far away from Him... is the place He has chosen to be.

Think of someone sitting up with a person they love, through a long and painful night. <short pause> They don't talk much. <short pause> They don't ask to be entertained, or thanked. <short pause> They pull the chair a little closer, and they stay. <short pause> If the one in the bed falls asleep, they stay. <short pause> If the one in the bed turns away, and faces the wall... still, they stay.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Let God be that close to you now. <short pause> You don't have to turn toward Him. <short pause> Just allow the chair to be there. <short pause> As you breathe in... the Lord is near. <short pause> As you breathe out... to my broken heart. <short pause> Again, slowly. <short pause> The Lord is near... <short pause> to my broken heart. <short pause> And once more, without the words... only the breath, and the nearness.

I'll pray for you now, and you can simply listen. <short pause> Father, be near to this child of Yours. <short pause> Be near when they first wake, and it all comes back. <short pause> Be near at the table, where a place is empty. <short pause> Be near on the birthdays, and the anniversaries, and the ordinary afternoons that hurt for no reason anyone else can see. <short pause> Be near when the visitors stop coming, and the cards stop arriving. <short pause> When Your child cannot hold on to You, hold on to Your child.

And Father, for the one they miss... <short pause> You know that life completely, every year and every hour of it. <short pause> We place that dear name into Your hands, where love is not lost. <short pause> Keep what we cannot keep. <short pause> And give Your comfort, a little at a time, as it can be borne. <short pause> In the name of Jesus. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: tender reassurance, very slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: If you felt nothing during that prayer, it was still prayed. <short pause> He is still close. <short pause> His nearness doesn't depend on your noticing it. <short pause> And you don't have to make do with only an unseen comfort. <short pause> Let someone sit in the real chair, too. <short pause> A friend, a pastor, a grief counselor, anyone who can stay a while... <short pause> and let you be sad.

parts.style: soft, very slow blessing, resting between phrases
parts.text: May the Lord be near you in the next hour. <short pause> May He be near you in the one after that. <short pause> And in every room that has grown too quiet... <short pause> may you find that you are not alone.
